_doc: The weather (Systems/Weather.cs): a pure function of the seed and the hour, never saved and never the town's dice. Pressure systems are born every `every` days (on average) upwind, anywhere across `reach` road days of the map, and drift `speed` road days a day toward the prevailing wind's bearing (a seed's own, swinging `swing` degrees over the year; each system wanders `steer` from it) for `life` days, swelling and fading. Each is `radius` days across its heart and `stretch` times longer across its path (a front). `lows` of them are lows of `strength` (the low end far commoner); the rest are highs of `highShare` that strength, which clear the sky. `great` is the share of lows by season that are great storms of `greatStrength`. Slow wet and dry spells of `spell` lie over the whole map for about `spellDays`. Heat: `mean` plus `swing2` round the year (warmest on day `warmest` of it), the map's warm side (`climateHeat` degrees at full, World.Climate) and the country's lean, plus `daily` round the day; highs bring frost in winter and heat in summer. Summer thunder: over land above `thunderAbove` degrees, `thunderPer` storminess a degree up to `thunder`, in the afternoon and in a cell here and not there. The storminess where each step begins (grey, foul, storm, tempest) is `steps`; a foul day with wind past `gale` is a storm, and on dusty ground a sandstorm. Below `snowBelow` degrees it snows; snow lies by `lays` a day by step and melts above `meltAbove` by `melt` a day. Ground remembers rain `wetDays` days, fading `wetFade` a day. The town reads the sky `lead` days ahead, `leadReader` more with a hero of the `readers` classes at home. A march toward the town takes a day more for each `marchSnow` mark of lying snow passed, `marchStorm` in a storm of `marchStormHours` hours or more (an afternoon's thunder doesn't), at most `marchMost`. Habitats and themes lean the weather: `wet` storminess, `heat` degrees, `wind`, `fog`, `mild` (the sea's share off the year's swing), `dust`, `sea`.

road._doc: Weather on the roads (Roads.Weathered, Weather.Slow, Venture.Exposed). Each stretch of a party's road is slowed by the sky over its middle when they walk it: `snow` of a day's march per unit of snow lying, `mud` per unit of wet ground past `mudAbove`, and `step` by the worst step (fair to tempest); an airship flies over the snow and mud but bucks the wind by `fly`. A stretch loses at most `most` of its hours again. Fog adds `fogDc` to the navigator's DC and a storm `stormDc`. A ford with ground wetter than `flood` is in spate: parties go round by a bridge if one can be reached. A night in the open at or below `cold` degrees, at or above `heat` by day, or in a storm or worse, calls for a Constitution save against `dc` (cold and heat) or `stormSave`; whoever is best at survival tries to make shelter (`shelterDc`) and gives them all the better of two dice. A failed save costs `die` per level band of the country.

snow: Snow lies deep on the road past {place}; they wade it and lose {days}.
The drifts past {place} cost them {days} of floundering.
storm: A {kind} catches them past {place}; they shelter and lose {days}.
They sit out a {kind} past {place} and lose {days}.
mud: The road past {place} is a bog after the rain; it costs them {days}.
Rain has turned the way past {place} to mud, and they lose {days} in it.
fly: Headwinds past {place} hold the airship back {days}.
The ship beats into a {kind} past {place} and loses {days}.
flood: {name} is in spate after the rain, too deep to wade; they go round by {bridge}.
The river runs high over {name}; they turn for {bridge}.
cold: Frost bites hard in the night, cold enough to kill.
heat: The day's heat is a furnace on the road.
The sun beats down without mercy all day.
stormNight: The {kind} rages all night over the camp.
They spend the night in the teeth of the {kind}.
shelter: {name} digs them a shelter in time ({roll}).
{name} finds them a lee and makes it snug ({roll}).
noShelter: {name} can find no shelter worth the name ({roll}).
hurt: Not all of them shrug it off: {list}.

harvest._doc: Weather influences the harvest, never decides it (Conner, 2026-10-23): a farm's yield is multiplied by Weather.Harvest, kept between `least` and `most`. Over growing land (the day's heat above `growFrom`) the month's wet ground (a reading every four days) below `dry` cuts up to `drought`; wetter than `soaked` cuts `soak`; kindly ground between `kindly` adds `kind`. Tuned so a year comes out about even: drought on about one growing day in twelve, kindly on one in three. A storm over the fields that day flattens `storm` of it, and a frost at dawn outside winter `frost`. The Ledger hears when the fields turn parched, sodden or kindly.

drought: No rain for weeks: the fields round {town} are parched, and the farmers watch the sky.
The ground cracks in the fields round {town}. The harvest will be thin if the rain holds off.
soaked: The fields round {town} lie waterlogged; the crops rot at the root.
Too much rain: the furrows round {town} run like ditches.
kindly: Kindly weather for the fields round {town}: sun and soft rain in turn.
The farmers of {town} say they have not seen a growing year like it.

damage._doc: Storm damage in town (Weather.Daily): on a day a storm with a gale is over the town each finished timber building has `storm` chance (a great storm `tempest`) of losing roof and walls, `wreck` of its work, at most `most` of them; stone stands. A thunderstorm has `lightning` chance to strike one timber building and fire it, `strike` of its work; slate and lime (Research.Fireproof) turn some away. Damaged buildings are mended as the town's repairs say (Simulation.SetRepairs).

storm: The {kind} tears at {town} and takes the roof off {list}.
Wind and rain batter {town} all day and leave {list} damaged.
lightning: Lightning strikes {name} in the {kind} and sets it ablaze; the rain puts it out, but not before it is gutted.
A bolt from the {kind} hits {name}; it burns until the rain beats the fire down.

lords._doc: Weather-working lords (Weather.Lords), from day `from`: a site whose master is one of `list` works the weather round its lair while it holds out: `storm` (thunder and wind), `fog`, or `winter` (`winter` degrees colder at the heart, snow), `power` at the heart over `radius` road days. A lord with a `call` sends a storm about every `every` days at the town or at a company on the road within `reach` road days of its seat: `power` and `radius` at its heart, crossing to its mark over the first part of its `hours`; riding a storm already brewing there multiplies it by `ride`. The town's answers: the `wardens` research turns called storms aside at once (and halves storm damage), a druid at home of `calmLevel` or more turns one with `calm` chance a day. `tamed` research softens the weather's cuts to the harvest by its share; `glass` research reads the sky a day further. Called storms are saved; lairs are refreshed each morning.

call: The sky darkens out of season. Riders say {lord} has called a storm, and it is coming for {town}.
Thunder rolls from a clear morning: {lord} sends a storm at {town}.
ride: A storm was brewing over {town}, and {lord} rides it in: it will be worse than any of the old folk remember.
{lord} takes the storm already gathering and drives it at {town}.
party: Word on the wind: {lord} has sent a storm after the {party} on the road.
The {party} write that the sky turned on them: {lord} has called a storm down on their road.
vane: The Storm Vane turns on its mast, and the storm {lord} sent breaks up before it reaches {town}.
The wind-wardens' vane swings round; the storm from {lord} veers off and blows itself out.
calm: {name} climbs the bell tower and speaks to the sky. The storm {lord} sent turns away from {town}.
{name} the druid walks out into the wind and sends the storm from {lord} back where it came from.

kinds.name: Clear
kinds.text: Clear skies and a light breeze.

kinds.name: Hot
kinds.text: Blazing sun: heavy going for anyone in armour.

kinds.name: Frost
kinds.text: A hard, clear frost. The ground rings underfoot.

kinds.name: Fog
kinds.text: Thick fog: hard to see who's coming.

kinds.name: Rain
kinds.text: Rain, and mud on the roads.

kinds.name: Snow
kinds.text: Snow falling, and lying on the roads.

kinds.name: Thunderstorm
kinds.text: Thunder and lightning, and rain in sheets.

kinds.name: Gale
kinds.text: A gale: no day for ships or fliers.

kinds.name: Sandstorm
kinds.text: A sandstorm: shelter or be flayed.

kinds.name: Great storm
kinds.text: A great storm, the kind the old folk date things by.

signs: The swallows fly low and the wind backs to the {wind}. The old folk of {town} say a {kind} is coming {when}.
A ring round the moon over {town}, and the cattle lie down in the fields: a {kind} is coming {when}.
Mares' tails high in the sky, and the smoke of {town}'s chimneys sinks to the street. The shepherds bring the flocks in: a {kind} {when}.
breaks: A {kind} breaks over {town}. Shutters bang, the market packs up, and the gutters run.
The {kind} reaches {town} on a {wind} wind. Doors are barred and the streets empty.
great2: A great storm falls on {town}, the worst in living memory. The wind screams through the streets and nobody sleeps.
The sky over {town} goes black at noon. A great storm, of the kind the old folk date things by.
clears: The storm blows itself out over {town}. People come out to count slates and sweep the lanes.
Blue sky over {town} again. The storm has gone on its way.
